body:
# aggregator(actions): cleanText caps can split a surrogate pair — a stored action field ends in a lone surrogate

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8a0a1c0cea`)

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts:289-292` — every user-supplied payload field of a dashboard action passes through:

```ts
function cleanText(v: unknown, max: number): string | undefined {
  if (typeof v !== "string") return undefined;
  const t = v.trim();
  return t === "" ? undefined : t.slice(0, max);
}
```

`slice(0, max)` counts UTF-16 code units. When an astral character (e.g. an emoji, 2 code units) straddles the cap, the stored value ends in a lone high surrogate. Call sites with caps: `reason` 2,000 (`actions.ts:336`), `text` 20,000 (`:334`), answer values 2,000 (`:376`), `optionId`/`questionId` 200 (`:349`/`:351`/`:363`/`:370`), `status` 60, `until` 64, and others (`:321`–`:450`). These values are persisted in the actions store (one JSON file, `PM_AGG_ACTIONS_FILE`) and consumed/rendered by the orchestration pass.

Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-actions-surrogate/probe.ts`, real `actions.ts` imported from the laptop primary, `validateNewAction` with verb `dismiss`):

- Input `reason` = `"x" × 1999 + "😀" + "tail"` (2,001+ code units) → validated `ok: true`; stored reason is exactly 2,000 code units and its last code unit is `0xd83d` — a lone high surrogate.
- `JSON.stringify` of the stored value ends `…\ud83d"` — the lone surrogate is carried into the persisted JSON.
- A UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip of the stored value differs from the original and ends in U+FFFD — any consumer that encodes the field to UTF-8 (file writes in other languages, GitHub bodies, Rust consumers, whose `serde_json` rejects unpaired surrogates) silently corrupts or refuses the field.
- Control: `"x" × 1998 + "😀"` (exactly 2,000 code units) is stored intact, length 2,000.

## Why it matters

This is the exact defect class fixed for pm-dispatch in #3178 (`validate.ts:319-328` keeps the cap but never leaves half a surrogate pair). The actions boundary was not given the same guard, so a dashboard user who pastes long text with an emoji at the cap boundary gets a silently corrupted reason/answer stored and delivered to consumers — and the corruption only surfaces downstream, far from the boundary that created it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cleanText` (or an equivalent shared helper) never returns a string ending in a lone high surrogate or beginning-of-cap lone low surrogate: when the cap would split a surrogate pair, the pair is dropped whole (cap becomes `max - 1` code units for that value), mirroring the #3178 fix in `pm-stack/dispatch/src/validate.ts`.
- The cap semantics otherwise stay identical: same maximum code-unit lengths, same trim/empty behaviour, non-straddling values byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/actions.test.ts` (or a sibling suite run by the aggregator test workflow): an astral character straddling at least the `reason` (2,000) and one small cap (e.g. `optionId` 200) boundary is stored whole-or-dropped, never halved; the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- Existing aggregator test suite stays green.
